## Glossary


**configFromSaved**  
Saved settings.json to full config: saved fields over the defaults, vendors merged mode by mode.

**ConfigRevisionError**  
Thrown when settings changed elsewhere since they were read: reload before saving.

**ConfigStore**  
Persists settings to disk with JSON patch semantics and revisions; the viewer reads and writes through it.

**database**  
Class: Postgres via Prisma (schema, db scripts, JSON helpers).

**defaultConfig / starterConfig / defaultAgents**  
Full defaults / minimal first-install bootstrap / the one bare executor.



**.foundry/audit.jsonl**  
Audit log: a before/after row per committed settings change (`GET /api/settings/history`).

**.foundry/project.json**  
A repository's committed project settings (e.g. `chorus`); machine settings win key by key.

**.foundry/settings.json**  
Runtime config: default provider/model, vendors, agents, composition, layers, sources, projects.

**foundry_test**  
The local test database: `bun run db:push:test` then `bun run test:db`.

**installationName**  
This Foundry's name, used by Kingdom pairing.


**journal.rawMiddlewareDays**  
Retention days for raw middleware journal rows (default 30).




**Prisma schema**  
`prisma/schema.prisma`: Entry only (the `postgres` memory tool's entries), on Postgres with pgvector.

**projects[id].agents**  
Project agents: standalone or `extends: <global id>` with optional `override`; never Wardens.

**validateAgentKinds**  
Refuses an agent in settings whose kind is not configurable: settings declare executors only, so a Warden is refused.


**settings**  
Class: the settings model: .foundry/settings.json, ConfigStore with patch semantics and revisions, resolution, settings routes.

**toPrismaJson**  
Converts a value for a Prisma JSON column (null becomes JsonNull); toOptionalPrismaJson leaves undefined unset.

**unwrapped**  
A thread with no layers, Warden advice or thread-state, only Foundry's standing session briefing: the fresh-install default (wrapsThread).

**validateConfig**  
Validates a full config: vendors, conversations, scheduler, agent kinds (executors only), main-thread labs, the subscription policy, projects and Kingdom settings.

**vendors**  
Settings key: each vendor on/off with a subscription mode and an API mode.


## 1. What this Warden covers

The settings model (`.foundry/settings.json`, how it is loaded over defaults, validated, saved with patch semantics and applied live) and Postgres through Prisma, which holds only the `postgres` memory tool's entries.

## 2. The domain

The `settings` class owns `.foundry/settings.json`. ConfigStore is the only writer: it persists with JSON patch semantics and revisions (a stale write raises ConfigRevisionError), and every committed change becomes a before/after row in `.foundry/audit.jsonl` (`GET /api/settings/history`, settingsChanges computes the per-definition diff); running threads take edited layers, agents and instructions on their next turn, while region, chorus-enable and provider changes apply to new threads. configFromSaved turns the saved file into a full config over defaults, vendors merged mode by mode; validateConfig checks the whole config (a new check goes into it), and an old key or kind is now just unknown. For defaults choose by scope: defaultConfig is the full default config, starterConfig the minimal first-install bootstrap for a chosen provider and model, defaultAgents just the one bare executor; a fresh install is unwrapped (wrapsThread) and everything else is opt-in. readRepositorySettings reads a repository's committed `.foundry/project.json` raw, reporting malformed files instead of throwing. Project agents (`projects[id].agents`) are standalone or `extends: <global agent id>` with `override`, and are never Wardens: settings declare executors only, so a Warden's kind is refused (validateAgentKinds). On the viewer side loadSettings fills the settingsConfig signal and the control, models and runtime route folders serve the settings endpoints.

The `database` class is small: the Prisma schema (Entry only, the `postgres` memory tool's entries, on Postgres with pgvector; nothing mirrors the journal into Postgres), `bun run db:push` for the configured database, `db:push:test` then `test:db` for the local `foundry_test` database. The tech stack is fixed: Bun, strict TypeScript, bun test, SQLite for the local journal, Prisma/Postgres only for the memory tool. The BullMQ job queue (removed in #209) and the logger adapters (removed in #213) are gone: Foundry calls `console` directly.

Many part-3 doc members are settings keys whose behaviour lives in another region; point there for the behaviour: `chorus.layers`, the warm-cache key and hand-named Warden refusal are `chorus`; `@inixiative/foundry/classify` and charters are `classify`; the composition view is `composition`; source versions and CompositionAuditor.recompose are `audit-log`; subagent child threads, middleware-reduced rows and the journal are `threads-journal`; the vendors registry is `models-providers`; the archive capture claim is `archive`. Not here: installing the daemon, doctor, `bun run setup` and last-good settings are `install-daemon`; the viewer's settings pages and server are `viewer`; test tiers other than `test:db` are `testing-vcr`.

**Source:** `CLAUDE.md` § Config (in "Foundry")

#### Config

Runtime config lives in `.foundry/settings.json`. A fresh install is one executor (`defaultAgents`: no instructions, inheriting the default provider and model) and nothing else, so its threads are **unwrapped**: no layers, Warden advice or thread-state reach the native session, only Foundry's standing session briefing (`wrapsThread` in `agents/thread-runtime.ts`). Everything below is opt-in. Foundry's own signals are written into the memory store only while a configured `file` source reads it.

It defines:
- Default provider/model
- Vendors (`vendors`): one per vendor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, ...), each on or off with a subscription mode (a native CLI login: Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code) and an API mode (an API key); a registry provider runs while its vendor and mode are on (`models/vendors.ts`).
- This Foundry's name (`installationName`), which Kingdom pairing uses
- Agent definitions: executors only (id, kind, provider, model, temperature, tools). An executor adds no instructions of its own: a main thread's come from its thread role. No Wardens: a Warden's kind is not one settings configure, so one in `agents` or `projects[id].agents` is refused
- The composition view (`composition`): the instruction ladder and what each role picks from it, thread roles included
- Layer definitions (id, maxTokens, sources)
- Data sources
- Project settings

The viewer dashboard reads and writes this config. `ConfigStore` handles persistence with JSON patch semantics.

A Warden is three parts: **instructions** and **domain knowledge**, both composed by the composition view, and **thread knowledge**, generated per thread by its post-work review. The composition view is one ladder that composes every slot for every role, main thread included ([usage-and-context.md](docs/usage-and-context.md), "Composition view"). Instructions are the generated agent's `prompt` (the generic region instructions plus its region's title and routing line), then the project's **Warden brief** (`.foundry/warden-brief.md`, a short high-level explanation of the project for Wardens, with a personal `.local.md`; its own ladder nodes, `agents/warden-brief.ts`), then its role files. Domain knowledge is its region's knowledge.md (a generated `domainKnowledge` source) plus its role files. **A Warden never gets the CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md ladder** (Aron, 2026-11-02): both slots take no general files, none arrives by an `@` import or a slotted source either, a `general` pick for a region role is not applied (reported in `view.chorus.ignoredComposition`), and nothing switches it back on. Both live in private layers, never on the thread's stack, and a Warden owns no configured layer. Each phase (advise, guard, review) appends its own response protocol, so a Warden prompt never states a JSON shape. Every Warden classifies through `@inixiative/foundry/classify` (`packages/foundry/src/classify/`), Foundry's one classification primitive, the same code live, in the evals and in Oracle's experiments: a run of at most three stages (`chorus.wardens.stages`; default the two-layer chain: Haiku 5.5 low pointing with its why inline, each yes escalated without it to Sonnet 5.5 low, Oracle finding `2026-11-01-l2-nowhy`; the single stage with API-token decisions), each naming its model and effort, the region doc it reads, its outcomes (binary or ternary), its reason (none, inline, followup), its task (recognise or point) and what it escalates. A pointing stage runs under the fixed Warden charter (`WARDEN_CHARTER`, `classify/charters/point.warden.ts`, composed above its instructions, never settings: point only, the main thread decides), a recognising stage under the recognise charter; charters are Foundry's per task and role, and refused in settings (each is named sections in committed files, `classify/charters/<prompt>/<section>.md`, which only an eval run's `sections` may set; a stage's modes, ternary or a why inline or asked after, add their own sections from `classify/charters/<prompt>/modes/<mode>/<name>.md`, each placed `after` a section or at the end, or, as an explicit dagger, `overrides` one, sent unless its file says `enabled: false`; the assembler itself holds no mode text). Each stage's response protocol is generated from it (the default is exactly the advice and guard protocols: pointer-only, guard findings advisory with no suggestion) and its answer read strictly, a malformed one counted, never guessed. Every Warden is asked at every trigger point that reaches it (`user-message`; `agent-action`, once per turn over the turn's whole tool activity when it ends, not per tool call, `guard: "per-call"` restoring a guard per call; `subagent-spawn`, a brief when the agent hands a task to a subagent; `consumed`, when the main thread takes in a ticket, spec, Linear issue or Notion page, opt-in per project with `chorus.consumed`; `milestone`, at a call that lands work (a pull request opened or merged, a publish, `set_status` done, a standing rule file written), on Claude before it runs as context beside the call; `hand-back`, over the message a turn that did work handed back, riding the next turn); there is no routing and no pre-filter (R-2026-11-19-04); `NO_COMMENT` is the expected answer and adds nothing to the thread ([FLOW.md](docs/FLOW.md#when-a-warden-weighs-in-the-charter-trigger-points-and-no_comment)). A Warden's advice is appended to the user's message as "The <domain> Warden chimed in:"; a handoff brief is appended to the subagent's own prompt (Claude) or rides with the parent's next message (Codex, Muse) as "The <domain> Warden chimed in on the handoff to <description>:".

A project's Wardens are its **chorus** (`projects[id].chorus`, over the repository's committed `<project>/.foundry/project.json` `chorus`, the machine's settings winning key by key), opt-in (`"enabled": true`; regions present but not enabled are reported as off), built from its concept regions, `<project>/.foundry/regions/<id>/{region.json,knowledge.md}` (`agents/region-roster.ts`, through `resolveProjectView`): one Warden per region, its knowledge the region's knowledge.md in full, run under the charter (an instruction to build is a reason to look; `NO_COMMENT`, or a pointer, ranked `Look over here: <name> (<where>) — <why>` then `Less likely: …`, an `All of these:` set, or a `Choose one:` sibling set unless a stage turns `pointer.any` off, at most three names; Wardens point, the main thread decides). A region declares its `role` (`warden` by default, or `herald`: the socket only, Heralds are not built and their regions never run); `stages` or `charter` in `region.json` are refused by name. Each stage's doc must be in every region of its role, or the chorus is not built and `view.chorus.missingDocs` names the region and doc; a region that can't be read or built (a malformed `region.json`, a source collision) likewise leaves the project without Wardens, the error as `view.chorus.reason`, because a repository's files never stop the daemon booting (Aron, 2026-11-16: on that day one project's region kept every Foundry with it registered down for five hours); each doc is its own source (`region:<id>`, `region:<id>:<doc>`), version and warm key. A later stage keeps its own primed session (`<thread>:aux:domain:<d>:stage:<n>`) and, on another model or effort, its own decision host; it gets a share of the trigger's deadline, and when it times out, fails or answers out of shape the previous stage's outcome stands, journalled (`classified` on the contribution). Only a pointing stage's yes reaches the thread. Two stages are the default; a project's written stages replace them. Region Wardens are the only Wardens: not enabled, or enabled with no regions, the project has no Wardens and the view says why (`view.chorus`: `on`, `enabled`, `enabledBy`, `reason`); a thread without a project has none. A thread of a running chorus holds the reception charter (`CHORUS_RECEPTION`, how to read a chime, including the acknowledgement rule for a system the instruction contradicts) once as a standing layer; `chorus.reception: false` leaves it out. A chorus may be layered (`chorus.layers`, in order: a later layer's region replaces an earlier one whole); each region has a warm-cache key, the content hash of its composed knowledge, journalled with every call (`versions.chorus`). There is no global setting. Org and personal `.foundry/roles/region/<region id>/` files overlay a region (a namespaced role's files nest by namespace). A captured rule goes to the thread's role; the person may apply it to one of the project's region Wardens instead (`feedback/routing.ts`, `wardenRoles(config, projectId)`). See [usage-and-context.md](docs/usage-and-context.md), "Chorus".

A project agent (`projects[id].agents`, never a Warden) is **standalone** (a full definition) or **`extends: <global agent id>`**. An extension appends its `prompt` (under a heading per chunk) and its `domainKnowledge` (source ids, each under its label) to the parent's, global first; `override: ["instructions" | "domainKnowledge"]` replaces that chunk instead. No entry means the global agent applies unchanged. `GET /api/projects/:id/resolved/agents` shows where each chunk came from.

Settings edits apply live: every committed change is a row in Foundry's audit log, `.foundry/audit.jsonl` (before/after per definition, `GET /api/settings/history`), and running threads take edited layers, agents and Warden instructions on their next turn. Adding or removing a region (or enabling the chorus), and provider changes, apply to new threads.

Every Warden call records what its instructions and domain knowledge were composed from, as version ids, not text (`audit/`, docs/THREAD-TREE.md spec B). The audit log holds a **source version** for every change to a source: a settings definition, a ladder file (`file:<path>`), a settings prompt (`prompt:agent:<id>`), a configured source's text (`source-content:<id>`), a feedback-written line, or the charter. Each row records the actor and the cause. The journal's `composition_version` lists a slot's parts in order (glue, source version plus the text it contributed, per-message text), so `CompositionAuditor.recompose` returns the exact text. Advice, guard and review requests carry `versions: {charter, instructions, domainKnowledge, retrieved?, chorus?}` (`chorus` is a region Warden's region and warm-cache key); text chosen per message is stored raw with the call.

A thread is a tree (docs/THREAD-TREE.md spec A).
- **Subagents.** The executor's native subagents (Claude Agent/Task, Codex sub-agents) are recorded as observed child threads (`turns/subagents.ts`), tied to their real parent by `handoff` / `handoff-return` rows. Every turn that would get injection calls the Wardens, subagents included (Aron, 2026-11-02): a Claude handoff (`Agent`/`Task`/`SendMessage`) is briefed at its call, before it runs, and the chimes ride into the text the subagent reads (`turns/handoff-brief.ts`, a `pre-use` `updatedInput`; an `advice` row on the parent, `trigger: subagent-spawn`); a Codex or Muse subagent is briefed when it starts and the brief rides the parent's next turn. Each subagent turn is guarded once when it ends, on the subagent's node, in every runtime.
- **Compaction.** When a turn closes, each middleware call gets a `middleware-reduced` row: its state (versions) and its result, never its input.
- **Retention.** Raw middleware rows age out after `journal.rawMiddlewareDays` (default 30).
- **Archive.** It gets reduced entries and per-node snapshots with `lineage`. Capture claims the native sessions it records, with a lease, so the Archive collector skips them unless Foundry dies before fulfilling.

<!-- unit doc:docs/SYSTEM.md#6-database-schema-prisma-schema-prisma -->
**Source:** `docs/SYSTEM.md` § 6. Database Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`) (in "Foundry System Documentation")

#### 6. Database Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`)

PostgreSQL with pgvector extension.

| Model | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `Entry` | Knowledge units (conventions, corrections, ADRs) with vector embeddings, the `postgres` memory tool's store |

The schema holds `Entry` only: the Postgres mirror of turns (`Trace`, `Span`, `Signal`, `Intervention`, `ThreadState`, `Message`) was dropped (#209). The local journal (`.foundry/sessions.sqlite`) is the record of every turn.

---

### 4b. Code entries

From the catalog (extracted from the code through the repo's Atlas map, described by a model). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.

#### Class `settings`
- **configFromSaved** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#configFromSaved` [primitive] turn a saved settings.json into a full config over defaults, vendors merged mode by mode Use: const config = configFromSaved(raw)
- **ConfigStore** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#ConfigStore` [primitive] persist settings to disk with JSON patch semantics for the viewer Use: new ConfigStore(configDir)
- **createProject** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#createProject` [primitive] build a project settings entry from just a path Use: createProject(projectPath, overrides?)
- **defaultAgents** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#defaultAgents` [primitive] give a fresh install its one bare executor with no layers or Wardens Use: defaultAgents()
- **defaultConfig** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#defaultConfig` [primitive] produce the default full Foundry configuration Use: defaultConfig()
- **loadSettings** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/ui/settings.js#loadSettings` [primitive] fetch /api/settings into the settingsConfig signal Use: await loadSettings()
- **readRepositorySettings** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config-resolve.ts#readRepositorySettings` [primitive] read a repository's .foundry/project.json, reporting malformed files instead of throwing Use: readRepositorySettings(projectPath)
- **settingsChanges** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#settingsChanges` [primitive] list per-definition differences between two configurations Use: settingsChanges(before, after)
- **settingsConfig** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/ui/settings.js#settingsConfig` [primitive] hold the loaded settings config as a reactive signal for the viewer Use: settingsConfig.value
- **starterConfig** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#starterConfig` [primitive] build the minimal bootstrap config for a new install with a provider and model Use: starterConfig(providerId?, model?)
- **validateConfig** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/config.ts#validateConfig` [primitive] validate a full config (vendors, conversations, scheduler, agent kinds, labs, subscription policy, projects, Kingdom) Use: validateConfig(config)
- **packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/control** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/control` [system] serve viewer HTTP routes for control settings Use: add control endpoints in packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/control
- **packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/models** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/models` [system] serve viewer HTTP routes for model settings Use: add models endpoints in packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/models
- **packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/runtime** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/runtime` [system] serve viewer HTTP routes for runtime settings Use: add runtime endpoints in packages/foundry/src/viewer/routes/runtime

#### Class `database`
- **bun run db:push** `package.json` [script] push the Prisma schema to the configured Postgres database Use: bun run db:push
- **bun run db:push:test** `package.json` [script] push the Prisma schema to the local foundry_test database Use: bun run db:push:test
- **bun run test:db** `package.json` [script] run the Postgres-backed tests against the local foundry_test database, one at a time Use: bun run test:db
